content_of_post_to_comment:
The strange thing about struggling with discipline is that most people already know what they're supposed to do. Almost nobody has to be convinced that sleeping more, exercising regularly and spending less time on their phone or starting earlier would improve their life.

That's why I've started doubting whether self-improvement sometimes overestimates the value of better advice. If knowledge were the missing piece, most of us would have changed years ago. Maybe the harder question isn't: " What should I do? " maybe it's: " Why does knowing so rarely become doing? ". Personally, that's the question that has become much more interesting to me and it completely changed the way i think about discipline. I stopped looking only for better advice and started paying much more attention to the invisible systems, environments and repeated decisions that shape behavior before motivation even enters the picture. I'm curious how other people here see it the same way. Have you ever reached a point where you realized you already knew what to do, but that knowledge alone wasn't changing your behavior? If so, what do you think was actually missing?
